vipāka:
[Vi+paca+ṇa]  CL=7 (1) The result or consequence corresponding to the action or deed. (2) The consequence of merits and demerits, particularly in the form of resultant mental aggregates (nāmakkhandha). (3) The result or consequence includes: (A) The physical identity or existence (attabhāva) arising from past kamma. (B) Expressions or designations arising from the ripening of kamma. (C) Objects experienced, whether pleasant or unpleasant. (D) Emotional states such as worry, weeping, and grief. (E) Outcomes such as pleasure, peace, or tranquility found in deva realms, human existence, or nibbāna. (4) Completion or accomplishment of the ripening process. (5) The threefold classification of results: Immediate result, Subsequent result, Later result. (6) The cause that leads to the ripening of consequences. (7) The process by which kamma influences physical digestion (metaphorically or literally). (8) Factors contributing to the ripening of results. (9) The occasion or chance for the arising of consequences. (10) Discourses or teachings about results or consequences (vipāka).
[Kaccaññaḥ. 529. Rū. 580. Vi+pāka. Aññamañña visiṭṭhānaṃ kusalākusalānaṃ pākāti vipākā. Abhi, ṭṭha, 1. 84. Visiṭṭhopākoti vipāko. Anuṭī, 1. 41. Aññamaññaviruddhānaṃ kusalākusalānaṃ pākāti vipākā. Vibhāvinī. 83. Maṇimañjū. 2. 36. Vipāka-saṃ. Vivāga-prā, addhamāgadhī.]
